AGENDA

Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Brotman asked staff to provide a brief report on some of the crime trends in
  Glendale. Police Chief Manuel Cid provided an update and stated that crime statistics remain
  low and that the City of Glendale is one of the safest cities in the US of its size. He expressed
  that the Police department focuses on crime reduction, traffic safety, and emergency
  preparedness. Cid mentioned there is an increase in grand theft auto in the Los Angeles
  County region and the statistics has doubled in Glendale from 2019-2020 but has remained at
  that level and is relatively steady. The other issue Cid mentioned is robberies. According to
  the Police department’s records, there was a steady uptick of robberies from 2018 and leading
  up to 2022. He highlighted some of the many reasons why there was an increase in these
  types of crimes – easier access to guns, zero-bail during the pandemic, estes robbery or petty
  theft escalated to robbery due to use of force, and a change in reporting crime in a more
  detailed fashion. Cid stated that the Glendale Police Department takes a proactive approach
  on everything they do and would like to have an increase in staffing to fill up vacancies. He
  talked about upgrading the PD’s software and programs and having a good partnership with
  the community. Councilmembers Devine and Brotman thanked the police department for all
  they do and Brotman asked staff to provide a quarterly report on crime statistics.

  Mayor Kassakhian thanked Police Chief Cid for the report. Considering the recent school
  shooting in Nashville, Tennessee, Kassakhian thanked the men and women in uniform for all
  they do to protect our community. He asked to have a discussion in the future with other
  elected officials and other agencies in the city about how we respond to emergencies and give
  parents, staff, and educators some assurances as to how prepared we are for these types of
  tragedies. Kassakhian asked staff for an update regarding a report on implementing a
  conditional use permit for gun stores, selling and storing guns as well as limiting several
  operations in the city. Community Development Director Bradley Calvert indicated a report will
  be brought to council in the coming weeks. Cid stated that a report will be presented to council
  regarding the buy-back gun program and a public service announcement video will be
  broadcasted on TV on the efforts the city does for emergency preparedness in collaboration
  with the community. Councilmember Asatryan thanked the Glendale Police Department and
  Police Chief Cid for his proactive leadership and for being approachable and personable to the
  public.

  Councilmember Asatryan announced that March 28 is the last day and the last council
  meeting of March marking Women’s History Month. She decided to conclude the month’s long
  celebration with some lightness and fun during the meeting today. She stated that watching
  children learn and be creative brings so much joy and her current hairdo is done by two
  talented little girls, Amasia and Sis. Asatryan stated that before children grow up to be
  successful contributing members of society, they need a supportive environment and develop
  their emotional worth. She indicated that it is also important to provide support to city
  employees in their personal lives when they become new parents. Asatryan asked staff to
  provide a report on family leave and menstrual leave. She recognized that there is a global

  4
   stigma around menstrual health, and she stated that she hopes the city treats this as a health
  issue and normalizes these conversations to break the stigma while providing the city
  employees a supportive work environment. Asatryan said that menstrual leave is becoming
  more common in Corporate America and other countries such as Japan, Indonesia, and
  Spain, and this is one of those areas where Glendale can serve as a model city for others to
  follow for wellness and support of employees. She stated it would be worthwhile for there to
  be a proactive engagement for more women employees with the city’s HR Director Paula
  Adams who has an open-door policy. Asatryan also asked council to discussed programming
  around Women’s Equity/Equality Day during this morning’s Joint Meeting with Supervisor
  Kathryn Barger. As staff look into organizing these programs, it is as important to provide
  support and programming internally for city employees as it is for residents, women business
  owners, and entrepreneurs. Asatryan had one nomination for commissioner that she will
  announce during next week’s meeting.

  Councilmember Devine attended the Cesar Chavez Celebration, Armenian Easter Festival,
  Unique Fest at YMCA, and the Cherry Blossom Festival. She stated that the diversity that we
  have is so important in our community and we are very lucky to have relationships with all
  these different cultures. Devine thanked George Saikali and Nora Yacoubian of Glendale
  YMCA and Michael Belzer of Shoseian Teahouse for organizing all these events.

  Asatryan had a meeting with City Manager, City Attorney, and staff regarding the selection of
  mayor and housing authority chair. She stated that staff presented a thorough rotation system
  and the different options of how this could be done. Asatryan asked staff to have similar
  briefings with all the councilmembers for clarification.

  Kassakhian attended the Cesar Chavez Celebration to remember the incredible work of this
  civil rights leader. To kick-off the event, he stated there was a community clean-up in the
  morning and everyone gathered at the Pacific Park Campus. He also attended the other
  events Devine attended. Kassakhian met with the Girl Scout Troop 1631 and the troop is in
  the process of collecting children’s books at Fire Station 21 for donations. He asked the public
  to contribute to this children’s book drive. The goal of the children’s book drive is to provide
  books free to families that are in need and encourage parents to read to their children.
  Hopefully, this will help children learn to read and foster a lifelong love of reading. Kassakhian
  announced that he attended the Mashdots College 30th Anniversary celebration. He also
  attended the event at My Soccer Store Burbank, organized by Louise Gill, where LAFC
  players were there to sign autographs after winning the Major League Soccer (MLS)
  Championship. Kassakhian stated the joint meeting with Supervisor Barger was short but a lot
  was discussed including homelessness throughout the county, the funds and programs that
  are available to better serve the unhoused population, issues regarding equity, programs
  promoting women’s businesses and equal rights, programs that support technology,
  Rockhaven, the lack of park space in South Glendale and how to utilize state funds to be used
  for recreation and open space in South Glendale. During the joint meeting, they also
  discussed the small business summit and the 2030 Census MENA designation for Armenians.
  Asatryan thanked Barger for sponsoring the small business summit.
